records.text: An Argent warhorse.
A crazed water spirit of Zul'Drak, a hostile elemental that raises a Water Wall in battle.
A Scourge carrion eater, an undead creature found in the courtyard at the Argent Stand, where Commander Falstaav wants the Scourge destroyed.
A rampaging Scourge geist in Zul'Drak, encountered among the undead in the courtyard near the Argent Stand.
An Argent Crusader serving in the forces at the Argent Stand, who fights with Crusader Strike and Turn Evil and takes part in the Crusade's parachute drops.

Quetz'lun's Spirit is Quetz'lun herself, a vengeful ruler of the underworld she created as she died, where she cursed her former worshippers to eternal torment. She treats mortals as insects and toys with those who serve her, while plotting revenge on her former prophet.
A Drakkari Snake Handler is one of Sseratus's Drakkari followers at his altar, grouped with his priests and champions among the followers Corporal Maga seeks to defeat.
Priests of Sseratus are followers found at the Altar of Sseratus, where Corporal Maga wants them put out of their misery. They cast Blood of Sseratus and Mind Blast.

Champions of Sseratus are followers found at the Altar of Sseratus, where Corporal Maga wants them put out of their misery alongside priests and Drakkari snake handlers. They fight with Blood of Sseratus and Cleave.

Commander Kunz directs Argent Crusade patrols from Argent Stand, assigning recruits to assist four outposts and report back. He expects prompt service and bluntly rebukes late patrols, warning that continued service requires a better showing.

An Argent Crusade soldier fighting the Drakkari in Zul'Drak warns others about the danger and says the force should withdraw to Justice Keep. In the field, the soldier remains alert and focused on the battle.

Captain Brandon is an officer in the Argent Crusade campaign who keeps his soldiers’ condition and morale in view. He recognizes that months of hard fighting and little sleep wear them down, and supports practical measures such as pain-relieving salve and raising the Crusade standard over the battlefield. He asks visitors to help maintain these supplies and support the troops.

Captain Grondel is posted in a waterlogged part of Drak'Agal. He grumbles about paperwork and the miserable conditions, yet stays focused on keeping Scourge from his post and clearing sewage elementals that disrupt his sector. He also looks for ways to support troops enduring the stagnant water, asking for dry fuel to build a fire, and seeks a useful count from the last skirmish.

At Drak'Sotra, Captain Rupert, a Forsaken, directs patrol work against the Scourge and nerubians. He holds burning fallen Argent footmen so they never rise as enemies a solemn duty, though the smell sickens even him, and has no patience for cowardice in his recruits. He also wants nerubian tunnels sealed before they can reinforce.

At Heb'Valok, Captain Arnath is a seasoned veteran who has taken part in dozens of conflicts. Since alchemist Finklestein arrived, Arnath has been ordered to gather ingredients for his work. He follows orders, but resents being kept from the front lines and hopes to return to direct combat; he asks for help collecting samples to save his men time.

Sergeant Stackhammer commands Argent soldiers fighting at the Altar of Sseratus and asks for help gathering them to report back. He is reluctant to leave while the fighting continues, and worries that the prophet at the altar will become a serious threat.

Commander Falstaav leads Argent forces at the Stand, where Scourge attacks keep his tired troops under pressure. He asks for help holding the courtyard and gives his soldiers parachutes against deadly sky-terror falls; grateful for assistance, he remains ready to put capable newcomers to work.

He identifies himself as a Zandalar representative at the Argent Stand, where he investigates the Drakkari's assault on Sseratus. Ubungo studies how the Scourge's damage has weakened wild gods and devises a way to blunt the prophet's power: elemental fluids dilute the mojo, while muddlecap fungus muddles the drinker's mind.

The Prophet of Sseratus is a boastful, aggressive leader who claims the wild gods' power has made his side all-powerful, even against the Lich King. He orders attackers at the altar killed and urges his brothers to drink deeply; his speech also welcomes more mojo.

Sseratus is a snake god whose altar stands in Zul'Drak. The Scourge's presence has weakened the land and, in turn, the wild gods, and the Drakkari exploit this to do evil things to them. Sseratus has a prophet at the altar, whom Hexxer Ubungo warns the Argent Crusade to avoid.

A Crusade recruit, one of the soldiers called up to fill gaps after heavy losses in the campaign. Shaken by a fierce battle with the Scourge, recruits panic and plead to leave, though with encouragement they find new resolve to fight and cleanse the place. Captain Rupert needs them ready to follow orders.

Corporal Maga is an Argent Crusade corporal at the Altar of Sseratus, intent on finishing the work there. Maga wants Sseratus's followers put out of their misery, would have hated to leave without finishing the job, and calls the situation "a fine mess."
Dr. Rogers is a physician with the Argent Crusade at Drak'Sotra. After the Scourge drove the force from the ruins, he asks for help finding and tending the wounded veterans who have not returned.

Crusader Jonathan is one of the wounded veterans lost in the fighting around Drak'Sotra. In his confused recollection, an explosion is the last thing he remembers; he needs aid after being found among the ruins.
Crusader Lamoof is one of the wounded veterans lost in the fighting around Drak'Sotra. Found among the ruins, he sighs and asks for help.
Crusader Josephine is one of the wounded veterans lost in the fighting around Drak'Sotra. Her brief recorded words convey overwhelming pain as she awaits aid.
A basilisk of Zul'Drak that strikes with a Venomous Bite.
A defeated Argent footman, a fallen soldier amid the fighting.
A withered Argent footman, still identified with the Argent forces despite his changed condition. He appears among the troops in the area's fighting.

Crusade Commander Korfax speaks as a leader whose forces are caught between the Scourge and the Drakkari, delaying their effort to join the forces in Icecrown. He says he warned the Highlord against coming. His blunt first reaction to saronite is that he has never heard of it and that it looks evil; he tests its toughness with his axe and reaper.

Rimblat Earthshatter, of the Earthen Ring, listens to the elements and believes the land is near death. He understands the Drakkari are killing their gods to gain power against the Scourge, but considers this short-sighted and ultimately self-destructive. His remarks are direct and grave.

Rayne serves with the Cenarion Circle in Zul'Drak. Faced with something that seems beyond nature's reach, she reacts with alarm. She recalls the Plaguelands and the Battle for Light's Hope Chapel, yet says the horrors in Northrend have proved worse.

Avenger Metz speaks with familiarity about the Holy Light, warning a “brother” against invoking it casually. His remarks are dry and impatient: he rolls his eyes, dismisses a guess-the-smell approach, and demands that visitors state their business.
Zul'Drak Rats are small critters found across Zul'Drak.

Apprentice Pestlepot is a gnome alchemist who boasts that the Pestlepots are a storied family and that their alchemy is unmatched. Though still an apprentice, Pestlepot claims exceptional skill. They serve Finklestein, who is preparing truth serum at Heb'Valok, and ask for basilisk crystals from Drak'Agal to support the work.

Alchemist Finklestein is an alchemist at the Argent Crusade post in Heb’Valok, where he works with a laboratory and helps the patrol. He is occupied with his research and needs careful, timely assistance to prepare a truth serum for questioning a Drakkari prisoner. He also tests prospective apprentices by asking them to learn the laboratory and gather ingredients; he treats that as a measure of their seriousness.
The Trapdoor Crawler is a burrowing beast found around Zul'Drak that hides underground until threatened.
Zul’Drak bats are found across several areas of Zul’Drak. They attack with a fatal bite when engaged.
Thrym, the Hope Ender, is an undead in Zul'Drak.

Eitrigg investigates saronite at the Argent Stand with Korfax, Rayne, Rimblat and Metz, drawing on their expertise, nature and elemental powers, and the Holy Light to learn the ore’s origins and why it matters to the Scourge. Captain Rupert directs collected saronite to Eitrigg and his colleagues for study. Eitrigg calls the ore evil and hopes they can unlock its secrets before it is too late.
Sky Terrors are aggressive undead found in numbers in the region.

Malas the Corrupter is identified by Sergeant Moonshard as the leader of Kolramas, the crashed necropolis. Moonshard describes Malas as gloating there and demands his head, marking him as a prominent Scourge adversary.
Hath'ar Necromagi are Scourge necromancers at Kolramas, where they raise fallen Argent soldiers and use them against their former allies. Sergeant Moonshard calls for their destruction.
Hath'ar Skimmers are undead creatures found in the Kolramas area.
Defeated Argent Footmen are fallen Argent troops found across multiple parts of the region.
A Scourged Argent Footman is an undead foot soldier found in Zul'Drak.

Sergeant Moonshard is stationed at Drak'Sotra amid the Scourge threat from crashed Kolramas. He orders the destruction of the Hath'ar necromagi and Malas the Corrupter; his reward dialogue reveals grief over fallen comrades raised by the Scourge and a determination to honor their memory.

Specialist Cogwheel is an inventive, reluctant specialist at Drak’Sotra, pressed into impossible tasks against the Scourge’s plague sprayers. She sees how Hath’ar webbing might foul their hover spells, then turns the gathered spinnerets and sprayer parts into a tangled skein thrower. The work is messy: she wonders how the webbing shoots, gets it stuck in her hair, and calls the parts disgusting before finding them useful. She is relieved when the sprayers are brought down and jokes about avoiding a plague spray.

A Drakkari water binder is one of the shamans who came down from Zul’Drak’s upper tiers to take control of water elementals in the Drak’Sotra Fields. The Argent Crusade considers that a dangerous threat and has ordered the binders killed before they can put elementals at its disposal.

Sub-Lieutenant Jax is an Argent Stand officer tasked with keeping Drakkari water binders from gaining control of water elementals. He treats that threat as a serious military concern and reports the results of operations to his commander.
Mossy Rampagers are sewage elementals fouling Captain Grondel’s sector in Drak’Agal. Grondel complains that they disrupt his military operations and orders them cleared from his battlefield.
Crusader Whathah is a crusader encountered in Drak’Agal.
A Zim'Torga defender is an elemental guard stationed in Zul'Drak who hurls Ice Boulders at foes.
A Jin'Alai Warrior is a humanoid fighter of Zul'Drak who hurls a thrown weapon at foes when engaged.
Known as the Captured Champion, this individual is found in Zul'Drak.
Footman Hordum is a named footman found in Zul'Drak.
Crusader Brune is a named crusader found in Zul'Drak.

Har'koa is a snow leopard goddess devoted to her children and concerned for the other gods. The Drakkari turn her magic against her offspring, and she seeks help freeing and restoring them. While bound by her subduers, she cannot discern the other gods' fates and asks allies to investigate Quetz'lun. She grieves fallen friends yet believes their spirits endure. She values those who aid the gods and fears for allies sent against the Prophet of Akali.
One of the claws of Har'koa's altar. Har'koa says her claws may still wear sacred adornments left by former supplicants, and they carry Har'koan Relics that Chronicler To'kini wants recovered.

The Cursed Offspring of Har'koa are beasts whom the Drakkari have transformed into monstrosities. Har'koa calls them her children and asks adventurers to use her whisker to free them from their nightmare.

Frozen Earth is an elemental found around Drak'Mabwa and the Frozen Reach. Element-Tamer Dagoda needs its essence to keep her elemental defenders strong, and Wind Tamer Barah needs elemental hearts from the area to collapse nerubian sinkholes. It hurls Ice Spike.
Hath'ar Broodmasters are hostile undead found in the Drak'Tharon area, who hurl Shadow Bolt and wrap foes in webs.

Rhunok's body is too far gone, and his spirit asks that it be awakened and his suffering ended before a new prophet rises. Awakened, Rhunok fights back, insisting a challenger must earn the right to kill him; his will to survive remains strong.
The Priests of Rhunok gather around the Altar of Rhunok, channeling power toward the prophet and smiting foes with Holy Smite.
Drakkari Bear Trappers are Drakkari humanoids encountered in the Zul'Drak region who throw things at their foes.
A humanoid known as the Prophet of Rhunok.
A Heb'Drakkar striker is a humanoid mounted fighter that dismounts to attack and mounts again when it breaks off the fight.
A beast known as a Scion of Quetz'lun.

Witch Doctor Khufu is a Drakkari witch doctor at Zim'Torga who seeks renewed contact with Zul'Drak's old gods. He asks others to disrupt rituals that obstruct his attempts to commune and to honor neglected gods with offerings. He mourns the Drakkari's destruction of the land's natural gods, warning that the power they gain is fleeting and its cost eternal.

Element-Tamer Dagoda helps defend Zim'Torga alongside Ahunae, using captured elementals and their essence to strengthen the settlement's defenses. He sees the Drakkari's enchanted guardians as a growing threat and works to blunt their forces. Though under pressure from attacks on several fronts, he stays wry and reassuring, comparing a hypothetical army of tiki warriors to the Scourge's endless waves.

Scalper Ahunae is a Zim'Torga quest giver who turns local threats into practical work: he wants Heb'Drakkar scalps and lends his own knife, while also asking for the elemental rifts near Drak'Mabwa to be sealed before they endanger his people. He also knows how to draw out the Drakkari leaders at Jin'Alai and seeks their treasures.

Kutube'sa is one of the Drakkari leaders at the Pools of Jin'Alai, whose treasure Ahunae seeks. His cry for the death of the Zandalari and their puppets marks him as an open enemy of Zim'Torga's side; he is confident that his cause cannot be stopped.

Gawanil is one of the Drakkari leaders at the Pools of Jin'Alai, and Ahunae seeks his treasure. He urges his followers to kill their opponents and take Zim'Torga back, making the settlement a clear focus of his campaign.

Chulo the Mad is one of the Drakkari leaders at the Pools of Jin'Alai, whose treasure Ahunae seeks. When confronted, Chulo boasts that the treasure will not be taken from him; his words show defiance and attachment to it.

Overlord Drakuru commands Scourge forces in Voltarus and serves the Lich King, whose blessing he says he has received. He tests recruits by putting them in command of his minions, praising ability while treating failure as intolerable. His larger plan is to build an army and conquer Gundrak, using abominations against the Drakkari and capturing their chieftains. He promises greater power to those who prove useful.
The Jin'Alai Medicine Men are stationed throughout Jin'Alai and channel shadow magic shortly after appearing.

Stefan Vadu is a death knight researcher at Ebon Watch who studies the blight affecting nearby scourged trolls. He creates an unstable Scourge disguise for fieldwork and relies on Nass, his blight-resistant companion, to collect troll hair samples. Stefan is fond of Nass and jokes that the companion finds his way home by smell; he warns others to treat the aging creature gently.
Withered Trolls are freshly scourged creatures near Ebon Watch, among those Stefan studies for the blight’s effects. They attack nearby targets with Withering Strike.

Chronicler To'kini is a Zandalari chronicler in Zul'Drak, gathering Drakkari artifacts and specimens of local wildlife for study with colleagues back home. He is curious about the Drakkari past and their relics, and regards their violent ways as a cause of their decline. His remarks frame the Zandalari presence as witness and record keeping as the empire nears its end.

Bloodrose Datura keeps watch at Ebon Watch and says she cannot leave her post, even when a signal flare suggests the Crusaders at Argent Stand may need help. She can demonstrate the danger represented by an Unliving Choker, and reacts with curiosity to some visitors and disgust toward a troll.

A captured Drakkari scout in Zul’Drak, he reacts with surprised gratitude when something is offered to him, calling it beautiful. His brief words give a personal glimpse of someone still capable of appreciation in captivity.

Rhunok is the spirit of an arctic bear god, separated from a body weakened by his former priests' attempt to channel his power through a prophet. The prophet absorbed too much power and died, and the priests resurrected him to continue their work. With his body near death, Rhunok asks those who aid him to awaken it with incense and end its suffering, fearing another prophet will rise and take his power. He thanks them and says Har'koa may have other plans, insisting that they are eternal.
A Scourge abomination at the Reliquary of Agony. Stefan in Ebon Watch wants the abominations there slain and their remnants brought to him.
A decaying ghoul among the undead in Zul’Drak, it is a rotting corpse animated to shamble through the area.
A hostile tormentor at Rhunok’s altar, it calls intruders filthy and orders them killed. It warns that Rhunok regaining strength would mean death for all, showing fear of the spirit’s return.
Gristlegut speaks in playful ghoul-directed baby talk, delights in a little ghoul, and feeds ghouls a special bowl of bowels and brains, joking that the meal makes friends.
A Guardian of Zim'Rhuk is an elemental that strikes foes with Whammy.
A roach-like creature found in the Grizzly Hills.
A Heb'Drakkar headhunter, this humanoid is encountered in the Grizzly Hills near Heb'Drakkar.
A stealthy Blightguard around Grizzly Hills, it uses invisibility before dropping concealment when engaged.
Baneflight is a flight master in the Grizzly Hills whose brief greeting asks where a traveler wants to fly.
Danica Saint is a flight master in Northrend. Her greeting asks travelers where they would like to fly, giving her a direct, practical role in regional travel.
Gurric is a flight master in Northrend. His greeting asks travelers where they would like to fly, giving him a direct, practical role in regional travel.
Maaka is a flight master in Northrend. The greeting asks travelers where they would like to fly, giving Maaka a direct, practical role in regional travel.
A caged geist, an undead creature kept under restraint.
Gorebag is an undead guide approached for a tour of Zul'Drak at Drakuru's direction. His replies are muffled, unintelligible sounds, and travelers can ask him to begin the tour.

The Prophet of Quetz'lun is the goddess’s power-drained prophet and an enemy who recognizes intruders from their earlier stealthy approach on a snow leopard. He resists Quetz'lun’s recovery of the power taken from him, pleading when she begins to reclaim it.
Quetz'lun is a wind-serpent goddess.

Overlord Drakuru presents the crusaders as an obstacle to his side's goal, looks toward Gundrak as destiny, and says the Lich King shares power with those who serve him. His words identify him with the Lich King's followers and connect his ambition to Gundrak.
Quetz'lun Worshippers are undead followers of Quetz'lun who take on Serpent Form in battle.
Serpent-Touched Berserkers are undead fighters marked by serpents, who strike their victim with Serpent Strike.
Blight Geists are blight-marked creatures whose speech comes out in rough, unintelligible sounds.

High Priest Mu'funu is one of the three priests Quetz'lun's Spirit orders punished at her altar, which places him in her service. He channels shadow magic and fights with Holy Smite, Power Word: Shield and Renew. At his defeat he cries out as Quetz'lun's Hex of Air is cast.

High Priestess Tua-Tua is undead and one of Quetz'lun's three high priests, alongside Mu'funu and Hawinni, whom Quetz'lun's Spirit seeks to punish with an empowered hexxing stick. She fights in Shadowform with Shadow Word: Death and Mind Blast, and cries out at fire when Quetz'lun's vengeance strikes her.
High Priest Hawinni fights with Serpent's Agility and can become enraged as his health falls. His brief associated cry is “BRRRRRR!”
A Flying Fiend, an undead creature found in Zul'Drak.
Blood of Mam'toth is a hostile living mass of blood that coagulates in a fight.
An Altar Warden guards the Altar of Quetz'lun. Har'koa wants the wardens there disrupted so that a Gusty Essence of the Warden can be recovered.
Fala Softhoof is a stable master whose recorded services include stabling pets and helping recover lost companions.
Marissa Everwatch is an innkeeper who welcomes weary travelers and offers her inn as a home, with goods for browsing.
Noggra is a general goods merchant in the settlement.

Darmuk is a hostile servant of Drakuru. When he sees through a disguise, he calls the intruder a “fleshling” and says their defeat will please Drakuru. Drakuru’s quest text blames Darmuk for watching over a failed blight batch.
Kevin Weaver is a trade goods merchant.
Arlen Brighthammer is a blacksmith who also offers goods and repair services. His work is practical and tied to maintaining equipment at the Argent Stand.
Haley Copperturn supplies engineering goods and also offers repairs. Her specialty is equipment for engineering, giving her a distinct trade among the Argent Stand’s merchants.
Claudia Bloodraven stocks leatherworking and skinning supplies at the Argent Stand. Her trade supports leatherworkers and skinners seeking materials for their crafts.
Alanna deals in jewelcrafting supplies at the Argent Stand. Her shop serves the needs of jewelcrafters, setting her apart from the other trade specialists there.
Aidan Steeleye supplies ammunition and also offers goods and repair services. His ammunition trade gives him a practical role among the Argent Stand’s equipment merchants.
Argent Stand Defenders are guards who help defend the Argent Stand.
Drakuru's servants are undead followers of Drakuru in Zul'Drak. They cast Rot Armor in a fight.
Drakuru's Guard is identified as one of Drakuru's guards, found among his forces in Zul'Drak.
Chad Carter is a trade goods merchant in Zul'Drak.
Amarante is a general goods merchant in Zul'Drak who also sells ammunition.
Vincent Huber is a reagents merchant in Zul'Drak.
Lessien is a tailoring supplies merchant in Zul'Drak.
Brady Ironcrock sells cooking supplies in Zul'Drak, stocking ingredients and kitchen provisions for cooks.
Lapu Stormhorn sells fish and fishing supplies in Zul'Drak to anglers.
Elizabeth Hollingsworth supplies ammunition in the Zul’Drak region and also offers repairs. Her services suit armed travelers who need to replenish their shot or have their gear repaired.
An armed defender stationed at Light's Breach in Zul'Drak.
Co'man sells reagents in Zul'Drak to those gathering magical components for spells and trades.
Ansari sells herbalism supplies in Zul'Drak to herbalists.
Saree sells alchemy supplies in Zul'Drak.
Ra'wiri sells general goods and ammunition in Zul'Drak.
Yamuna sells trade supplies in Zul'Drak.
Chin'ika is a Poison Supplier who sells poisons.
A Bloated Abomination, an undead creature found in Zul'Drak.
A Drakkari humanoid designated a Skullcrusher.
A humanoid Prophet of Har'koa in Zul'Drak who fights with a stunning Concussion Blow.
Enraged mammoths roam Zul'Drak, wild and hostile until the medallion's magic calms them into friendliness.
A dead Mam'toth disciple lies among the dead in Zul'Drak, a fallen member of the faith named for Mam'toth.
Ba'kari is a weapons merchant in Zul'Drak, specializing in maces and staves. Visitors can browse his goods.
Mam'toth disciples are found in Zul'Drak.
A guardian of Zim'Torga, one of several posted to keep watch in Zul'Drak.
An armed guardian who defends the Ebon Watch settlement.
In Zul'Drak, Corrosion supplies alchemy goods to visitors.
At Ebon Watch, Spiked supplies general goods and ammunition.
Mulch supplies herbalism goods in Zul'Drak.
Deathdrip supplies poisons at Ebon Watch.
Corpsedust supplies reagents at Ebon Watch.
Scabbard sells blades and repairs equipment. Customers can browse the goods, making Scabbard both a weapons seller and a repair contact.
Squirmworm is a trade supplies merchant, offering goods for customers to browse.
Shalewing is an undead creature found in Zul'Drak.
Enchanted tiki warriors serve as the warlord's special guardians at Zol'Maz Stronghold. Their potential mass production by the Drakkari is described as a serious threat.
A captured Drakkari chieftain held by the Scourge, he pleads to be released and questions why a visitor who is not Scourge can walk freely nearby.

Warlord Zol'Maz is a Drakkari warlord at his family's stronghold, carrying the key to Akali's chains. He reacts with fury to an enchanted tiki, accusing its bearer of killing his family, and threatens to kill them.
Tiri is Warlord Zol'Maz's wife and lives with him at the family stronghold.
Yara is Warlord Zol'Maz's daughter. When engaged, she calls out “Daddy!” and uses Sprint, showing her direct family tie and active participation in the fight.
Drek'Maz is Warlord Zol'Maz's son and part of the family gathered at the warlord's stronghold.
A Blightblood Troll, an undead troll that stays passive.
Akali speaks as a captive just freed from chains, then threatens the Drakkari for their past trespasses.
Akali Subduer is a fighter who hurls Fireball from a distance and, when badly wounded, wards itself with Mojo Empowered Fire Ward.

Overlord Drakuru boasts of building a Scourge army to sweep Zul'Drak, then reacts angrily when betrayed. He urges use of the Scepter of Domination and says the Lich King had great plans for his listener, revealing his investment in that scheme and his certainty about their shared destiny.
A slime found at Kolramas in Zul’Drak.
A lost Drakkari spirit found in the local area. It periodically manifests Spirit Particles, a visible effect that marks its spectral nature.
A restless, disturbed soul of Zul'Drak that strikes at its foe with Shadow Word: Death as a fight begins.

Sergeant Riannah is the flight master stationed at Light's Breach. Travelers from several distant outposts are directed to report to her, and her replies acknowledge reports from Kunz and Valus. Her brief warning captures the danger of her post: “Look sharp. It's life or death out here!”

Magister Teronus III is a Kirin Tor magister who can offer a teleport to Dalaran. He explains that the city has moved to Northrend and directs a traveler onward to deliver his signet to Archmage Celindra at the Violet Gate.
A Drakkari humanoid.
A hostile Gundrak savage who fights with Savagery.
A hostile Gundrak brute who fights with Brute Force.
A hostile Gundrak fire-eater who breathes flame with Flame Breath.
The Icepaw Bear is a bear in Zul'Drak.
The Frost Leopard is a leopard in Zul'Drak.
A hostile Gundrak bat rider who gets off its bat when a fight begins.
A Gundrak raptor is a wild animal in Zul’Drak. It attacks with a jump when fighting.
An Icetouched Earthrager is an elemental of Zul'Drak that brings down an Avalanche on its foes.
A Rageclaw Berserker, a humanoid fighter of the Rageclaw.
A Rageclaw Primalist, a humanoid of the Rageclaw.
A Rageclaw Hunter, a humanoid hunter of the Rageclaw.
A Drakkari snake found in Northrend.
A Vargul Deathwaker, one of the Vargul. Gerk at Thrym's End blames the Vargul for his brother's death and names Algar as their leader.
A Vargul Runelord, one of the Vargul. Gerk at Thrym's End blames the Vargul for his brother's death and names Algar as their leader.
A Vargul Slayer, one of the Vargul. Gerk at Thrym's End blames the Vargul for his brother's death and names Algar as their leader.
A Vargul blighthound, a beast tied to the Scourge's base at Thrym's End, where Engineer Reed wants wrecked Scourge scrap metal to get the tank running.
Vargul Plaguetalon is an undead creature found in Zul'Drak.
Burr is a friend of Crusader MacKellar at Crusader Forward Camp, lost when Prince Navarius and the Scourge attacked; MacKellar fears he was taken to Thrym's End.

Gerk is a survivor of the attack at Thrym’s End, grieving his brother and Dargath and fearing he is turning. He asks for vengeance on the Vargul and speaks of their experiments and the Lich King’s rejected. His words are strained by grief, but he still wishes the listener well.

Crusader Dargath is remembered by MacKellar as the man who urged the others out of the tank and charged when the group was attacked. Gerk later describes Dargath as a paladin who made a heroic stand against Algar. These accounts present him as courageous, though both come from others.
Pan'ya is an innkeeper who welcomes weary travelers and offers her inn as a home, with goods for browsing.
An undead banshee of Zul'Drak that unleashes a Banshee Wail.

Gymer is the King of Storm Giants, imprisoned by the Scourge after his brother Thiassi lured him into a trap. He fears becoming undead like other storm giants and seeks to drive the Scourge from Zul’Drak, especially those who have devastated his people. He describes himself as honorable and promises to aid those who free him. He speaks angrily to his Vargul captors and looks to his brothers for help.
A Drakuru creature of Zul'Drak that drains its foes with Blood Leech.
A Drakuru berserker of Zul'Drak that stamps its foes with Dire Stomp.
Ragemane is Chief Rageclaw’s trusted lion seal. Chief Rageclaw says Drakuru’s trolls turned Ragemane against him and, sorrowfully, asks that the animal be killed; Ragemane is found at Rageclaw Lake.

A Rageclaw wolvar held prisoner by Drakuru’s trolls, this captive is bound in chains and kneels. Its angry cries curse the trolls and promise revenge for the Rageclaw; once free, it turns its fury on its captors.

Crusader Lord Lantinga serves the Argent Crusade in Zul’Drak, where he tracks Drakuru’s threat and the destruction around Rageclaw territory. He sends Drakuru’s orders to Stefan Vadu at Ebon Watch and urgently dispatches aid to the Crusader Forward Camp. With much of his army occupied at Argent Stand, he seeks help from the nearby Knights of the Ebon Blade, whose members he recalls from Light’s Hope with open reluctance.

Engineer Reed works at the Crusader Forward Camp, hoping to repair a tank with Scourge scrap so the camp can oppose Prince Navarius's zombie production. He admits uncertainty about whether the plan will work. Freeing Gymer sounds risky to him, but he agrees to help if the storm giant will fight Navarius. Reed devises seaforium explosives to weaken the giant's cage and hopes Gymer will honor the bargain.

Crusader MacKellar survived Prince Navarius's attack on the Crusader Forward Camp. He praises Dargath's courage in charging out of the tank to protect the others and seeks help finding Dargath, Gerk and Burr. Alarmed by the surrounding Scourge, he warns allies to watch their backs. He honors his friends' sacrifices and is determined that they will not be in vain.

Chief Rageclaw is a wolvar chief who calls himself the smartest of his people. Drakuru's trolls drove the Rageclaw from their den and imprisoned some of his people; the loss of his seal Ragemane, a gift from his brother-in-law, leaves him grieving and unwilling to trade with trolls.
Drakuru Prophet is an undead combatant that casts Plague Cloud.
A Drakuru Raptor is a beast that attacks with a jumping strike when engaged.

Moky is the Rageclaw's top shaman, tasked by the chief with studying fire. After trolls drove the Rageclaw from their den and set it ablaze, he offers an extinguisher and asks for help putting out the fires. His study finds, with wry understatement, that fire burns.

Prince Navarius is one of the Scourge foes Gymer names for vengeance in Zul'Drak, alongside Algar and Thrym. Speaking to Gymer, Navarius dismisses his rescue as only delaying his death and reconstruction; as he dies, he calls on Thrym to avenge him.
A young Rageclaw creature, identified as a pup.
Algar the Chosen is a Scourge leader in Zul'Drak, named with Navarius and Thrym among the foes Gymer wants destroyed in vengeance. He fights with a Dreadful Roar.

Vargul Doombringer is a Vargul combatant who threatens Gymer in battle. He boasts that he will eat Gymer's heart or feed him to the dogs, insults him as a sniveling pig and maggot, and orders him to die.
A hound that fights alongside the Vargul, wounding foes with Broken Bone.
Vargul Deathwaker is an undead Vargul combatant who casts Plaguebolt in battle.
Vargul Runelord is an undead Vargul combatant who wields Rune of Destruction in battle.
Vargul Slayer is an undead Vargul combatant.
Banshee Soulclaimer is an undead banshee who uses Banshee Wail in combat.
Vargul Plaguetalon is an undead combatant in Zul'Drak who uses Swoop in battle.
A reanimated undead corpse found in Zul'Drak. It is one of the Scourge's risen dead.
An undead Acolyte of Agony in Zul'Drak.
Acolyte of Pain is an undead.

Gurgthock is a flamboyant, money-minded fight promoter who says he followed the gold from Nagrand to Zul'Drak. He presents the Amphitheater of Anguish as a lucrative spectacle, with Wodin as his bodyguard, and loudly hypes its fighters and bouts. He recognizes a former Ring of Blood champion and sees returning competitors as a draw; his interest remains fixed on the gold.

Wodin is a troll who serves as a bodyguard at the Amphitheater of Anguish. The arena's fight promoter identifies Wodin as his guard while explaining the matches, placing Wodin beside the action rather than in charge of arranging fights.
Asgari is a stable master in Zul'Drak, associated with pet stabling and the recovery of lost companions.
A snack seller at the Zul'Drak amphitheater, calling out to the crowd that snacks are for sale.
An Amphitheater spectator among the crowd around the fights in Zul'Drak.
Zena is Wodin's warrior kitten.
An Amphitheater spectator in Zul’Drak.

Elder Tauros recalls a time when people hunted for glory and honor, then wonders whether it is really different now. His conversation also lets visitors ask about seven other elders, tying him to a wider circle of elders.
Rafae is a flight master who offers fast travel. When provoked, he calls an enraged gryphon and wyvern into the fight.
Nofal sells ammunition and general goods, and repairs equipment.
After Akali's death, Tol'mar breaks his oath to observe only and calls for Gal'darah to pay. He describes the event as a dark day in troll history and says he cannot bear to watch.

Chronicler Bah'Kini is a troll historian at Dubra'Jin, west of Gundrak, recording the Drakkari Empire's collapse for future generations. She sees the trolls' destruction of their own gods as history repeating itself and hopes a clear account will keep others from following the same path. To'kini is her father and long-time teacher; she calls him cowardly for sending her to a post so near Gundrak. She studies the recovered tablets and unusual golem remains.
A Zul'drak Sentinel, an elemental that fights with Stomp and Whammy.
Griegen is an undead who roams several parts of Zul'Drak and hits hard with Smash.
The Terror Spinner is a beast of Zul'Drak that fights with impairing and instant poisons.

The Zul'Drak Flame Warden tends the Alliance festival flame, welcoming visitors who come to honor it and urging them to honor fires across Alliance lands. During the Midsummer celebration, the warden also encourages desecrating Horde fires.

The Zul'Drak Flame Keeper tends the Horde festival fire in Zul'Drak and urges visitors to honor Horde fires across Horde-settled lands. The keeper also encourages the desecration of Alliance fires, reflecting the conflict between the factions during the festival.
A male frost leopard, a beast whose native combat behavior uses Rake.
A male icepaw bear of Zul'Drak, an angry beast that claws its foes with Claws of Ice.

Ha'wana is a quest giver at Dubra'Jin who asks for Gundrak raptor eggs for Bah'Kini's sacrifices to Dubra'Jin. He explains that the offerings bring Dubra'Jin's aid against the Drakkari and wonders what the loa does with so many eggs. His speech uses a colloquial troll-like dialect.
Gondria is a rare, powerful beast found in several parts of Zul'Drak.

place_records.text: You are in Zul'Drak, a region of Northrend. The Alliance holds a few places here, chiefly The Argent Stand, while Ebon Watch, Light's Breach, Zim'Torga and Dubra'Jin belong to neither side. Scourge undead, Drakkari trolls and the followers of Sseratus fill the land, and Argent Crusade patrols fight them. Zul'Drak bats with fatal bites attack anyone who comes near.

You are in The Argent Stand, an Alliance stronghold in Zul'Drak. Commander Kunz directs Argent Crusade patrols from here, and Commander Falstaav leads the Argent forces through Scourge attacks. Magister Teronus III, a Kirin Tor magister, can send travelers to Dalaran. The stand also has its inn.

You are in the Altar of Sseratus, where Argent soldiers fight followers of the snake god Sseratus. Priests, champions and Drakkari snake handlers hold the ground around the altar. Sergeant Stackhammer worries that the prophet here will become a serious threat, and he is reluctant to leave while the fighting goes on.
You are in Drak'Sotra Fields, an open stretch of Zul'Drak. Crazed water spirits roam it, and Drakkari water binders try to bend the water elementals to their will.

You are in Drak'Sotra, a former Argent Crusade post in Zul'Drak that the Scourge overran. Captain Rupert directs patrols against the Scourge and nerubians here. Wounded veterans are still missing in the ruins, and withered Argent footmen, nerubian cocoons and Hath'ar broodmasters remain.
You are in Drak'Agal, a waterlogged part of Zul'Drak. Captain Grondel holds a post here, where stagnant water and sewage elementals disrupt his sector. Lurking basilisks also roam the district.

You are in Heb'Valok, an Argent Crusade post in Zul'Drak where the alchemist Finklestein has set up a laboratory. Captain Arnath, a seasoned veteran, gathers ingredients for him and resents being kept from the front lines. Trapdoor crawlers lurk in the area.

You are in Kolramas, the crashed necropolis of the Scourge in Zul'Drak. Malas the Corrupter leads the Scourge here, and plague sprayers and Hath'ar skimmers fill the ruin. Necromagi raise fallen Argent footmen from the dead.
You are in the Reliquary of Agony, a site in Zul'Drak where Scourge creatures gather. Decaying ghouls, plagueroaches and putrid abominations roam it.

You are in Ebon Watch, an outpost in Zul'Drak that neither side holds. Stefan Vadu, a death knight researcher, studies the blight on the scourged trolls nearby, and Bloodrose Datura keeps watch and can demonstrate the danger of the Unliving Choker. Its merchants sell reagents, blades and poisons.

You are in Thrym's End, a camp in Zul'Drak where Vargul blighthounds and deathwakers prowl. Gymer, King of the Storm Giants, is held prisoner by the Scourge, and Gerk survived the attack that took his brother.
You are in the Reliquary of Pain, a Scourge-haunted site in Zul'Drak. Flying fiends and blight geists drift through it, and a captured Drakkari chieftain is held here by the Scourge.

You are in Rageclaw Den, where Rageclaw berserkers, primalists and hunters live among the trolls. A captive Rageclaw wolvar is chained here by Drakuru's trolls, and Drakuru Blood Drinkers and berserkers roam the den.

You are in Light's Breach, a settlement in Zul'Drak. Chief Rageclaw is here with his people after Drakuru's trolls drove the Rageclaw from their den and set it ablaze, and Elder Shaman Moky still seeks help putting out the fires. Crusader Lord Lantinga of the Argent Crusade tracks the troll threat from here. There is a flight master, repairs and vendors.
You are in Pools of Zha'Jin, part of Zul'Drak. A lost Drakkari spirit lingers here and periodically manifests spirit particles. Disturbed souls haunt the pools.
You are in Zim'Abwa, part of Zul'Drak, where Drakkari natives are the local danger.

You are in the Amphitheater of Anguish, a fighting arena in Zul'Drak. Its fight promoter, Gurgthock, followed the gold here from Nagrand and stages the bouts, with the troll Wodin as his bodyguard, and a vendor sells snacks to the crowd. Lurking basilisks, mossy rampagers and Zul'drak sentinels are the dangers nearby.

You are in the Altar of Rhunok, in Zul'Drak. The spirit of Rhunok, an arctic bear god, lingers apart from his weakened body while his former priests channel his power into a resurrected prophet. Priests of Rhunok, Drakkari bear trappers and elemental rifts are the dangers here.

You are in the Altar of Har'koa, in Zul'Drak. The snow leopard goddess Har'koa is held here by her subduers, and the Drakkari have turned her offspring into monstrosities. Cursed offspring, claws of Har'koa and Har'koan subduers are the dangers here.

You are in Zim'Torga, a settlement in Zul'Drak that neither side holds. Element-Tamer Dagoda and Scalper Ahunae defend it with captured elementals, and the Drakkari witch doctor Khufu seeks contact with the region's old gods. It has a flight master, an inn, repairs, a stable master and vendors. Jin'Alai warriors are the danger nearby.
You are in the Pools of Jin'Alai, in Zul'Drak. Jin'Alai warriors and medicine men are the main dangers, with frost leopards and the troll Chulo the Mad among the rest.

You are in the Altar of Quetz'lun, in Zul'Drak. The spirit of Quetz'lun, the wind serpent goddess, rules the underworld she made as she died, where she treats mortals as insects and plots revenge on her prophet. Her worshippers, altar wardens and serpent-touched berserkers are the dangers here, with High Priestess Tua-Tua among them.
You are in Heb'Drakkar, in Zul'Drak. Heb'Drakkar strikers and headhunters are the dangers here, and the blood of Mam'toth, a mammoth god who destroyed himself, still lives on in the area.

You are in Drak'Mabwa, in Zul'Drak. Overlord Drakuru is here, a servant of the Lich King who looks toward Gundrak. Priests and prophets of Rhunok, along with frozen earth and elemental rifts, are the dangers here.
You are in Zim'Rhuk, in Zul'Drak. Guardians of Zim'Rhuk are the dangers here, along with frozen earth and elemental rifts. Overlord Drakuru is found in the area.

You are in Altar of Mam'toth, an altar in Zul'Drak. Dead Mam'toth disciples, Mam'toth disciples, enraged mammoths and Gundrak raptors are the dangers, and Zul'Drak bats here bite fatally when engaged. Overlord Drakuru says the Lich King shares power with those who serve him, and looks toward Gundrak as destiny.

You are in Mam'toth Crater, an area of Zul'Drak where Blood of Mam'toth and Mam'toth disciples are the dangers. Gondria, a powerful named beast, is a rare elite creature found in several parts of the region.
You are in Zol'Maz Stronghold, a place in Zul'Drak. Enchanted tiki warriors fill it, and Warlord Zol'Maz is among the foes here.
You are in Zol'Heb, a place in Zul'Drak. Gundrak fire-eaters, brutes, savages and raptors are the dangers here, along with terror spinners.

You are in Gundrak, a place in Zul'Drak. Gundrak fire-eaters, brutes, savages and bat riders are the dangers, along with Akali Subduers. Akali, a captive freed from chains, threatens the Drakkari for their past trespasses, while Overlord Drakuru looks toward Gundrak as destiny.
You are in Frigid Breach, a place in Zul'Drak. Drakkari skullcrushers and bloated abominations are the dangers, and servants of Drakuru are about.
You are in The Dead Fields, a place in Zul'Drak. Reanimated corpses and banshee soulclaimers haunt it, with vargul slayers, vargul blighthounds and Prince Navarius among the dangers.

You are in Dargath's Demise, a place in Zul'Drak where vargul slayers and banshee soulclaimers are the dangers. Crusader Dargath is remembered as a courageous man who charged out of the tank to protect the others.

You are in Crusader Forward Camp, a camp in Zul'Drak with repairs and a merchant. Engineer Reed works here, hoping to repair a tank with Scourge scrap, though he is unsure it will work. Crusader MacKellar survived Prince Navarius's attack and is alarmed by the Scourge around the camp.

You are in Dubra'Jin, a troll settlement in Zul'Drak with a flight master, repairs and a merchant. Chronicler Bah'Kini records the Drakkari Empire's collapse, believing that trolls turning on their own gods repeats history. Tol'mar, after Akali's death, calls for Gal'darah to pay.

You are in Voltarus, an area of Zul'Drak. A captured Drakkari chieftain is held here by the Scourge, and he pleads to be released. Blight geists, flying fiends and blightblood trolls are the main dangers, and Overlord Drakuru's guards and caged geists add to them.
